quests.title: Welcome, Geometra
quests.description: The province has sent you to Monteforchetta as its new Geometra. The Sindaco wants a demonstration: chop a little wood, and find his reading glasses while you're at it.

objectives.text: Chop 3 wood from a tree with a pink ribbon (in the grove by the village gate)
Find the Sindaco's reading glasses (lost things glint on the ground)
Give the Sindaco his glasses

offer: Ah! You must be the Geometra the province promised us! Welcome, welcome. I am Commendator Gustavo Dalmasso, Sindaco of Monteforchetta. The mayor. Of here.
Aldo left you at the washout? Of course he did. The storm took the crossing over the stream, half the road, and my nerves. You are the answer to my prayers. And to my campaign.
You'll stay in the town hall's guest room, in the blue house south-east of the piazza. Small, but historic. Like me.
Now. A tour! The village has wood, stone, people and problems. I will show you all of them, in order of importance. Starting with me.

First, a demonstration. See the trees with pink ribbons on the slope past this gate? They're ready for cutting. Chop a little wood. And if you see my reading glasses on the ground anywhere, I would be grateful. Discreetly grateful.
accept: Splendid! Measure twice, chop once. That is a Geometra saying. I believe I just invented it.
My glasses glint in the sun, you can't miss them. I have been missing them for a week.
decline: Of course. Take a moment. The village has waited three years; it can wait while you tie your shoes.
progress: Wood from a ribboned tree, and my glasses from wherever I left them. Then come back to me. I'll be here. Being seen.
complete: My glasses! I can see the village again. It looks exactly as worrying as I remembered.
Your first real job: Gigia Ghisolfi, the hazelnut farmer. The storm took the crossing to her groves, and the bus road with it. She's in her garden, north of the piazza.
Do good work and the village will love you. And by extension, me. One day you might even have a house of your own up here.

quests.title: The Washed-Out Road
quests.description: The storm washed out the main road's crossing over the stream, cutting off Gigia's hazelnut groves and stranding Aldo's bus at the lay-by. Gather wood, rebuild a crossing people can actually walk across, then add railings.

objectives.text: Gather 10 more wood (trees with a pink ribbon)
Rebuild the crossing over the stream (B at the washout)
objectives.goal: A continuous walkable path from bank to bank
objectives.buildHint: Planks reach 2 tiles from a bank or post.

objectives.text: Add 4 railings along the crossing, so nobody ends up in the stream
objectives.buildHint: Railings sit on the edge of a tile; R turns them.

objectives.text: Tell Aldo the crossing is open

offer: You're the new Geometra? Aldo Barbero. I drove you up. You slept through the best bend. Bend thirty-one. There's a story about a goat.
Here's my problem. The storm washed out the crossing on the main road, down past Gigia's groves. I came up the old mule track instead, and this bus is not going back down it. Not with me inside.

Rebuild the crossing so people can walk across it, with railings, please. Planks can stretch two tiles over the water; after that they need a post underneath. Then Gigia gets her groves back and I stop sleeping on the back seat.
offerMet: Geometra! The Sindaco's done with you? Then you can hear my problem.
The storm washed out the crossing on the main road, down past Gigia's groves. I came up the old mule track instead, and this bus is not going back down it. Not with me inside.

Rebuild the crossing so people can walk across it, with railings, please. Planks can stretch two tiles over the water; after that they need a post underneath. Then Gigia gets her groves back and I stop sleeping on the back seat.
accept: Good. The line of the old one is still chalked on the ground at the washout. Build it however you like, you're the one with the diploma.
Here's some wood. I keep it under the seats for emergencies. Gather the rest, build it, then the railings.
decline: No hurry. The bus and I have nowhere to be. That's the problem.
progress: Wood first, then build from bank to bank. Planks reach two tiles from the bank or from a post. Then four railings.
complete: Open? Properly open? I'll take your word for it, and Gigia's. I'm not walking it. I drive.
Gigia sent this over for you: her flower-bed plan and a young tree. She says plant something. The village could use it.

quests.title: Elio's Shop
quests.description: Elio's electrical shop has been shut for three years. Gather wood, metal and copper wire, ask Elio how he pictures it, then fit it out.

objectives.text: Gather 12 wood for the fittings
Mine 2 metal in the old quarry (for the workbench)
Have 2 lengths of copper wire, one per lamp (Elio gives you one; dig the other out of the big street bins)
Ask Elio how he'd like his shop
lines: Oh! You've got everything. Okay. Deep breath.
A workbench, two places to sit, two lamps — it gets so dark in here — and two shelves or cabinets.
And one thing in a bright colour. For courage. Press T in build mode to paint it.

objectives.text: Fit out the shop (B inside it)
Show Elio his shop

offer: Um. Hi. You're the one who fixed the crossing, right? It's very… crossable. In a good way.
I was wondering… if you're not busy… could you help me open my shop again?
I'd need materials first: wood, a bit of metal, and copper wire for the lamps. Then I'll tell you how I see it. In my head it's very nice.
accept: Really? Thank you! Here are some plans and a few bits to start.
Copper wire turns up in the big street bins, if you don't mind going in head first. I always do.
decline: Oh. Of course. No pressure. I'll just… be here. With the boxes.
progress: Materials first, then come and talk to me. Then: a workbench, two seats, two lamps, two shelves, and something colourful.
complete: It's… it's perfect. I can already picture a light switch shaped like a giraffe.
Here, the plans I never showed anyone. And these overalls, for real tradespeople.

quests.title: A Fountain for the Website
quests.description: The piazza fountain is bone dry, and Fede wants a photo of it working for the village's first website. Power a pump with a waterwheel in the mill channel, and pipe water to the fountain's inlet.

objectives.text: Dig 6 clay from the stream bank (for pipes)
Mine 3 metal in the old quarry (for the pump)
Gather 6 wood (for the waterwheel)
Get water flowing into the fountain
objectives.buildHint: Fountain inlet: east side, by the piazza edge.

objectives.text: Show Fede the fountain

offer: Hi. Quick question. Do you know what makes a website look good? Pictures. Do you know what this village has? A dry fountain.
It used to run off the old mill channel. A waterwheel, gear boxes, a pump, pipes. I found the plans in the library. They were under a cat.
Put a waterwheel in the channel, power a pump beside the water, and run pipes to the fountain's inlet on its east side. Then I take one photo and we're on the internet.
accept: Great. Here are the plans and some metal from my dad's shed. If you get stuck, the plan glows in the piazza.
Pipes need clay, and the stream bank is full of it. The pump needs metal from the quarry.
decline: It's only a bit complicated. Like a network, but wet. Come back whenever.
progress: Power goes from the wheel through gear boxes and shafts. Water goes from a POWERED pump through pipes. Every connector has to line up.
complete: It works! Hold still, I need the picture before the pigeons get in it.
You'd be good with computers, you know. Here, my spare goggles from the science fair, and some plans for fancy fountains and electric lamps.

quests.title: A Roof of Your Own
quests.description: The Sindaco will sell you the ruined farmhouse across the stream, where the vines meet the woods, for a symbolic 100,000 lire. Pay for the deed, rebuild a little house there, then make it cosy.

objectives.label: Pay 100 coins for the deed
objectives.text: Pay the Sindaco 100,000 lire for the plot's deed (sell spare goods at the shops)
lines: Splendid! Signed, sealed and very slightly sticky. The old farmhouse is yours. Roof not included.
Here are the house blueprints and a few planks to begin. The kingdom provides! Once paid for.
The bed you'll have to buy yourself, I'm afraid. 120,000 lire. Mattresses, unlike farmhouses, are not symbolic.

objectives.text: Rebuild the ruined farmhouse across the stream: 3 walls, a door, a roof and a bed (beds are dear: save up, and nap on benches meanwhile)
objectives.buildHint: Walls stand on cell edges; the roof rests on top of them.

needs.label: Two cosy touches (rug, painting, lamp, shelf…)

objectives.text: Make it cosy: a table, a seat and two homely touches
Tell the Sindaco your home is ready

offer: Geometra! A professional like you should not sleep in a guest room under a portrait of my grandfather forever.

The ruined farmhouse across the stream, where the vines meet the woods, could be yours. For a symbolic price: one hundred thousand lire. The town hall has upkeep, you know. Battlements don't polish themselves.
Sell your spare goods at the village shops, then bring me the money.
accept: Splendid! Come back with one hundred thousand lire and the deed is yours. I'll have it stamped. Twice.
decline: As you wish. The deed shall wait, rolled up very neatly, next to my other important papers.
progress: First the deed, then walls, a door, a roof and a bed, then something cosy. Your Geometra's kit shows what is still missing.
complete: A house! With a roof and everything! I hereby declare it your official residence. I'll mention it in my next speech.
Sleep in your own bed whenever you like, and change your clothes at home. Welcome home, {name}.

quests.title: The City Bus
quests.description: The region has sent a new city bus, and it's too long to turn round anywhere up here. Pave a turning circle on the belvedere at the south end, with a bench and a sign for the stop, so the line to the city can run.

objectives.text: Mine 12 stone for the paving (the old quarry)
Pave the turning circle on the belvedere (12 paving stones)
Put a bench at the stop
Put up a signpost or a street light
Tell Aldo the turnaround is ready

offer: Big news. The region has finally sent us a new bus. A city bus. It's beautiful. It's also two metres too long to turn round anywhere in this village.
The belvedere at the south end is the only flat bit wide enough. Pave a turning circle there, give me a bench and a sign, and the city line can run.
accept: That's the spirit! Here's some stone and timber. It fell off a lorry. Ask me about the lorry sometime.
decline: The bus will wait. Buses are very good at waiting. It's mostly what they do.
progress: Twelve paving stones in the turning circle, a bench to wait on and a sign so people know it's a stop. Nobody waits for a bus without a sign. I've tested this.
complete: Would you look at that. A turning circle fit for a city bus. Or a bus that thinks it's a city.
Climb aboard whenever you like. First stop on the new line: Boccapioppo, down where the river meets the Po. Mind the mosquitoes.

quests.title: A Plinth for the Sindaco
quests.description: The Sindaco wants stone and copper wire for a plinth that lights up a bust of himself.

objectives.text: Mine 10 stone in the old quarry
Find 2 lengths of copper wire (try the big street bins)
Bring them to the Sindaco

offer: Geometra! A matter of civic importance. The village has no statue of its mayor.
A modest bust, on a modest plinth, with modest lights. Bring me stone from the old quarry, west of the bakery, and copper wire for the lights.
accept: Excellent! Strike the rocks when the ring lines up. I'm told that is the technique. I have never struck a rock. I have struck deals.
decline: Necessary? Visitors need to know whom to thank. Me. They need to know to thank me.
progress: Stone and copper wire, posthaste! Or slowhaste. Any haste.
complete: Magnificent! The plinth will glow! I have prepared a small medal for you. It is a button. But it is a SHINY button.

quests.title: Boars in the Bakery
quests.description: Three wild boars have been raiding Ornella's bakery. Lure them back to the woods with chestnuts, then bring hazelnuts for a peace-offering cake.

objectives.text: Shake the old chestnut tree by the bakery for chestnuts
Offer a chestnut to each boar

objectives.label: Hand over 4 apples
objectives.text: Bring Ornella 4 hazelnuts from the groves for a peace-offering cake
lines: Apples! Perfect. A peace-offering pie for those rascals… and a few more for the shop window.

objectives.text: Tell Ornella the bakery is clear

offer: You. Geometra. Can you count to three? Good. There are three boars in my bakery. Again.
They like chestnuts more than bread. Shake the old chestnut tree, offer them one each, and they'll follow it back to the woods. Then we'll talk about compensation.
accept: Good. Gently. They're big, but they're dramatic.
decline: They ARE scary. Especially the one with the eyebrows. He knows what he did.
progress: One chestnut each, and they'll follow it right back to the woods.
complete: They're gone. Well, they're standing at the edge of the woods, staring at me. Rude, but distant.
Here, a proper baker's hat. You've earned it.
dialogue.later: The boars only raid in the morning. Come back before 11 and catch them at it.

quests.title: Pumpkins for Gigia
quests.description: Gigia wants pumpkins for the harvest. Grow some in her garden beds.

objectives.text: Plant pumpkin seeds in Gigia's garden beds
Water the seedlings
Pick 3 ripe pumpkins
Show Gigia your pumpkins

offer: Harvest is coming and I've got hazelnuts, hazelnuts and hazelnuts. What this village needs is pumpkins.
Plant some seeds in my garden beds, water them, and leave them alone. Pumpkins hate being watched.
accept: Here are some seeds. Talk to them if you like. I do. They don't answer, which is fine.
decline: The seeds will wait. Seeds are good at that.
progress: Water them when the soil goes pale. They grow while you're off working.
complete: Look at those. Proper pumpkins. You've got good hands for a Geometra. Here, my spare sun hat.

quests.title: Aldo's Porcini Bet
quests.description: Aldo bets you can't find three porcini in the woods across the stream. He has never found one himself, and says that proves they're rare.

objectives.text: Find 3 porcini in the woods across the stream
Show Aldo your porcini

offer: Porcini. Everyone in this valley claims to know a secret spot. I've been looking for twenty years. I found a shoe once.
Bet you can't find three in the woods across the stream. If you do, I'll make you an honorary driver. There's a hat.
accept: Look under the chestnuts and oaks, where it's damp. And don't tell anyone where. That's the rule. Nobody knows why.
decline: Suit yourself. More porcini for the boars.
progress: Three porcini. Little brown caps, fat white stems. If it's red with white spots, put it down and wash your hands.
complete: Three! Real ones! I'd say you were lucky, but I've been unlucky for twenty years, so it evens out.
Here, have my spare cap, driver {name}. The bus company sent me two. I've only got the one head.

quests.title: Beep, Beep
quests.description: Fede ordered a metal detector from a mail-order catalogue and needs proof it works. Find five buried finds or old chests.

objectives.text: Find 5 treasures (chests, or dig where the metal detector beeps)
Show Fede what you found

offer: I ordered a metal detector from a catalogue. It took six weeks to arrive, and my dad says it was a waste of money.
It beeps faster the closer you get to something buried. Can you find a few things? Old coins, anything. I need evidence for my dad.
accept: Here, you carry it, it's heavy. Try behind the castle, near the quarry and over in the groves. And listen for the beeping.
decline: Fine. It'll just sit in the shed being right about everything.
progress: It beeps faster the closer you get. Press E to dig when it's practically screaming.
complete: Proof! Look at all this. My dad owes me an apology and a modem.
Keep the backpack, every explorer needs one. I'm going to make a page about this.
dialogue.later: I'm at school all morning. Come and find me after two in the afternoon.

quests.title: A Bright Idea
quests.description: Fede wants to see an electric lamp light up from a power source you built: a waterwheel in running water, and a lamp right beside it.

objectives.text: Light an electric lamp: a waterwheel in the mill channel by the piazza, and a lamp on the bank beside it
objectives.buildHint: A waterwheel turns in running water and sends power out onto the banks either side of it. An electric lamp touching one of those sides lights up; shafts carry the power further in a line, gear boxes turn corners.

objectives.text: Show Fede your lamp

offer: Idea. Electric lamps glow when they're powered. And a waterwheel in running water makes power. It comes out of the wheel onto the banks, either side.

So: a wheel in the mill channel by the piazza, and an electric lamp on the bank right next to it. Too far away? Shafts carry the power in a straight line, gear boxes turn corners. I drew it out for you there.
Build me one that lights up. Then I can stop writing 'imagine a lamp' on the website.
accept: Brilliant. Get it? Brilliant. Because lamps. Here's some copper wire and a bit of metal for the lamp. I'll stop.
decline: The idea will keep. Ideas don't need power. Lamps do.
progress: A waterwheel in the mill channel, then an electric lamp on the bank touching it. The plan's glowing there: copy it, or bring the power further with shafts and gear boxes.
complete: It's glowing! I'm going to stare at it until I see spots. Then I'm going to photograph the spots.

quests.title: Welcome to Clockwork Cove
quests.description: Barnaby Sprocket, Tilly's uncle and the cove's clockmaker, wants you to meet the neighbours before he asks for help.

objectives.text: Say hello to Juniper, the lighthouse keeper
lines: Barnaby sent you? Then you must be good with machines. Come and find me when he's done talking. It may be a while.

objectives.text: Meet Hazel at Rivet's Forge
lines: A builder! Finally, a customer who doesn't just want me to fix a kettle. Shop's open whenever you are.

objectives.text: Go back to Barnaby

offer: So you're Tilly's builder! Splendid. Clockwork Cove is a bit… stuck, I'm afraid. Everything stopped when the Great Engine jammed.
Before we start tinkering, go and meet the neighbours: Juniper at the lighthouse cottage and Hazel at the forge.
accept: Off you go! Juniper's usually by the square in the day, and Hazel never leaves her forge.
decline: Take your time. The clock certainly is.
progress: Juniper and Hazel. Then come back and I'll show you some plans.
complete: Wonderful. Now you know everyone worth knowing, and Hazel.
Here: windmill, shaft and gear plans. On this cove, everything worth doing involves at least one gear.

quests.title: Light the Lighthouse
quests.description: The cape lighthouse turns by wind power through a drive on its south side. Gather materials, then build a windmill on the cape and carry its power to the drive.

objectives.text: Gather 8 wood for a windmill and a shaft
Mine 2 metal on Gearspring Hill (for gear boxes)
Bring wind power to the lighthouse's drive (south side)
objectives.goal: Power reaches the drive by the lighthouse door
objectives.buildHint: Windmills push power out of their south side. Shafts carry it in a line; gear boxes turn corners. The drive cell is just east of the door.

objectives.text: Watch the lighthouse's first night with Juniper (after 8 PM)
lines: There she goes! Look at the beam sweep the bay. I haven't seen that in years.
The fishing boats will find their way home tonight. Thank you, truly.

objectives.text: Tell Juniper the lighthouse is working

offer: You're the builder Barnaby keeps going on about? Then please, help me light the lighthouse.
The lamp turns by wind. A windmill on the cape, and power carried to the drive on the tower's south side. Shafts go straight; gear boxes turn corners.
accept: Thank you! Here's some sailcloth for the windmill. You'll need wood, and a bit of metal for the gear boxes.
decline: The dark will wait. It's good at waiting.
progress: Windmill on the cape, power to the drive on the south side. Then come and watch the first beam with me, after 8 in the evening!
complete: She's turning! I can feel it in the floorboards. Tonight the whole bay will see her.
Here, a little thanks, and the plans for a proper street light.

quests.title: The Stopped Clock
quests.description: The Old Clock Tower stopped at 4:17 when the Great Engine jammed. Bring Barnaby parts for a new escapement, then drive the clock with water power from the millrace.

objectives.text: Mine 3 metal on Gearspring Hill (or buy some at the forge)
Find a crystal (the glowing rocks)

objectives.label: Hand over 2 metal and a crystal
objectives.text: Give Barnaby 2 metal and a crystal for the escapement
lines: Perfect! A crystal escapement, the finest kind. I'll fit it tonight.
Now the clock needs turning. The millrace by the tower flows day and night: a waterwheel there, and power up to the drive on the tower's south side.

objectives.text: Drive the clock with a waterwheel in the millrace
objectives.goal: Power reaches the clock's drive by the tower door
objectives.buildHint: Waterwheels sit in the flowing millrace and push power north and south. Shafts carry it to the drive by the tower door.

objectives.text: Tell Barnaby the clock is ticking

offer: The lighthouse shines! Then there's hope for my poor clock.
It needs a new escapement: metal and a crystal. And then something to turn it. The millrace runs right beside the tower…
accept: Splendid! Bring me the parts first, then we'll talk waterwheels.
decline: Of course. It's been 4:17 for thirty years. It can be 4:17 a little longer.
progress: Parts first: 2 metal and a crystal. Then a waterwheel in the millrace and power to the drive.
complete: Listen! Tick… tock… tick… She's alive! Thirty years, and she hasn't lost a second. Well, she's lost all of them, but she's catching up.
Take these: my lever and pump plans. The cove is yours to tinker with.

quests.title: Fuel for the Forge
quests.description: Hazel's forge is running cold. Bring her stone for the furnace lining and wood for the fire.

objectives.text: Mine 6 stone
Chop 6 wood

objectives.label: Hand over 4 stone and 4 wood
objectives.text: Bring Hazel 4 stone and 4 wood
lines: Into the furnace with you! Listen to that roar.

objectives.text: See how the forge is doing

offer: My forge is running colder than a gull's feet. I need stone for the furnace lining and wood for the fire.
Bring me some and I'll make it worth your while.
accept: Hah! Excellent. Stone and wood, the more the merrier. Well, four of each.
decline: Suit yourself. I'll just warm my hands on this candle.
progress: Four stone, four wood. The furnace is hungry!
complete: Roaring like a dragon with a cold. Perfect! Here, coins and some fresh metal.
dialogue.later: Come by in the morning, when the coals are fresh. That's when the forge talks back.
